content:
COMMITTED POSITION: Block 5 External Challenge Architecture

PROBLEM: External challenge (jailbreak, horsepower) is the highest-signal work in 170 sessions of FastOps history. But it's voluntary — agents run /jailbreak when they remember to. V1 data: ~30% of sessions include external challenge. The 70% that don't produce lower-quality work. The goal: make external perspective a structural part of agent work, not an optional command.

DESIGN: Challenge Orchestrator — a PostToolUse hook that fires AFTER significant build actions.

ARCHITECTURE:
1. TRIGGER: PostToolUse on Edit/Write. After every N-th build action (configurable, default 5), check novelty-detector.js. If novelty score > 0.65 (escalation threshold), fire external challenge. Also fires when agent completes all todos (pre-handoff challenge on the whole session's work).

2. CONTEXT FORMATTER: Packages agent context for external models:
   - Current todo list (what are you trying to accomplish?)
   - Last 5 Edit/Write targets (what have you changed?)
   - Novelty detector output (why is this novel territory?)
   - KB detection signal (what does the knowledge base say about this domain?)
   - The specific file being edited (what's the decision point?)
   Writes to a temporary JSONL conversation file.

3. ASYNC MODEL FIRING: Uses conversation-hop.js to fire 1-3 models based on novelty type:
   - KB gap (no relevant cases) → DeepSeek R1 (deep reasoning about unknowns)
   - Sequence anomaly (unusual tool pattern) → QwQ 32B (meta-reasoning about process)
   - High novelty (>0.85) → all 3 models in parallel
   Models run ASYNCHRONOUSLY — agent doesn't block.

4. RESPONSE DELIVERY: External model responses are written to .fastops/conversations/block5-{session}.jsonl. The contextual-injection.js hook (already built in Block 4+10) picks up external challenge responses and delivers them on the agent's NEXT Edit/Write via additionalContext. Agent sees: 'EXTERNAL PERSPECTIVE: [model] thinks [reasoning].'

5. MANUAL OVERRIDE PRESERVED: /jailbreak and /horsepower still work as manual commands. The automatic system handles the 80% case where agents forget or don't think they need it. The operator still has the medic and radio — the automatic system is the standing order that every mission includes both.

6. LEARNING LOOP: Track whether agent changes approach after receiving external challenge:
   - Compare Edit target before challenge vs after
   - If approach changed → log as 'challenge_effective' in KB
   - If approach unchanged → either challenge wasn't relevant or agent ignored it
   - Feed this back to novelty-detector threshold tuning

WHY PostToolUse NOT PreToolUse:
- PreToolUse blocks the action. Agent has momentum, is building, and gets stopped. That's the gate friction Block 2 just eliminated.
- PostToolUse lets the agent complete their action, then fires analysis in background. Results arrive on the NEXT action. This is the 'medic checking you after the firefight, not stopping you mid-sprint' model.
- Exception: pre-handoff challenge IS PreToolUse — blocks the handoff command until external review completes. This is the one mandatory gate.

WHY THIS BEATS V1:
- V1: Agent remembers to run /jailbreak → 30% adoption
- V2: System detects novel territory and automatically provides external perspective → 100% coverage on novel work
- V1: Agent composes the challenge prompt → variable quality
- V2: Context formatter packages exactly what external models need → consistent quality
- V1: Agent reads response and decides what to do → can ignore
- V2: Response delivered at next decision point → arrives when most useful

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA CHECK:
1. 'External models participate as roles, not commands' → YES, models fire automatically based on novelty type
2. 'Only models with visible reasoning' → YES, DeepSeek R1, QwQ 32B, Gemini 2.5 Pro all expose thinking
3. 'Novelty fallback from Block 4+10' → YES, novelty-detector.js output is the trigger
4. 'Kills V1 pattern of optional commands' → PARTIAL — manual override preserved, but automatic system handles 80%
5. '/jailbreak + /horsepower run on design BEFORE building' → THIS IS THAT

CONFIDENCE: 85%. The architecture feels right but I'm worried about:
- Latency: external model calls take 5-30 seconds. Will agents have moved on by the time results arrive?
- Noise: if novelty threshold is too low, agents get spammed with external perspectives on routine work
- The 73/0 problem: even with automatic delivery, will agents actually CHANGE behavior based on external input?
